title: Can it rain frogs?
summary: Josh and Chuck explore whether it can really rain frogs (and fish, snakes and other things). They survey historical reports, from Athenaeus's account of frogs in Dinar, Turkey, to dubious claims like the Bergen lemmings, and Charles Fort's "super Sargasso Sea" theory. They then cover the real Serbian frog rain of 2005 and the waterspout explanation first proposed by Andre Marie Empire, including how waterspouts form and why the animals are often a single species. They also discuss an unusual-updraft explanation and a Louisiana fish-rain sighting. The episode closes by linking the biblical Ten Plagues of Egypt to a proposed climate-driven chain of events, and ends with a listener mail about a military family who listens to the show.

segments.title: Opening banter and frog-themed merchandise
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the episode on raining frogs, joking about frog-themed mouse pads and umbrellas and the 'raining men' search results.

segments.title: Historical reports of strange rains
segments.summary: Josh lists historical reports of unusual rain: Athenaeus's account of frogs and fish near Dinar, Turkey; Bergen, Norway in 1578-1579; Memphis, Tennessee in 1877 with snakes; Pliny the Elder's blood, flesh and wool; and many other cases including maggots, jellyfish, and tadpoles. He notes that some reports are discredited.

segments.title: Dubious reports and Charles Fort's theory
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how many old reports rested on people assuming animals fell from the sky without witnessing it, including a London-area doctor's garden story. Josh describes Charles Fort's idea of a suspended 'super Sargasso Sea' dumping its contents as rain, from The Book of the Damned.

segments.title: Frog rain in Serbia and the snake tangent
segments.summary: The hosts note a documented 2005 case in Serbia where people saw and heard frogs fall during a storm and hit roofs. Chuck tells a story about catching a copperhead near his yard, which leads into a joke about listener mail.

segments.title: Waterspouts and Andre Marie Empire's explanation
segments.summary: Josh explains that French physicist Andre Marie Empire attributed the phenomenon to waterspouts, which pick up light creatures from water and drop them over land as pressure drops. Chuck asks for the mechanics.

segments.title: How waterspouts form
segments.summary: Josh explains tornadic and fair-weather waterspouts, and how warm rising air and sinking cold air create a low-pressure vortex that can lift objects. He notes the lifted objects can include animals, and the hosts discuss how tornadoes lift larger things.

segments.title: Why one species at a time and other updraft theories
segments.summary: The hosts discuss why reports usually describe a single species. A Washington University professor suggests similar size and weight, and a Southern Illinois professor proposes that any unusual updraft at about 60 mph can do it. A Louisiana wildlife department worker reported fish raining at about one per square yard.

segments.title: Skeptical wrap-up on frog rain
segments.summary: Josh says the simplest explanation is a waterspout picking up and dropping animals, and frames this as part of a trend of explaining biblical events. Chuck says he would need to see it to believe it.

segments.title: Explaining the Ten Plagues of Egypt
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a Telegraph article by science correspondent Richard Gray suggesting a climate shift around Pi-Ramesses in the Nile Delta, which could have triggered the plagues in sequence. They cover the Nile turning to blood via algae, frogs, flies and lice, disease and boils, hail and locusts, and darkness from a Thera (Santorini) eruption, with the firstborn deaths possibly from grain fungus. They are skeptical of some links.

segments.title: Episode wrap-up
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck sum up the episode and note that the frog-rain question comes down to a waterspout explanation, with some skepticism remaining. They point listeners to howstuffworks.com for more.

segments.title: Listener mail from a military family
segments.summary: A listener mother describes how the podcast has become part of her family's life, including her son's interest in Kiva microloans and animal topics, and her Marine husband's listening while deployed. The hosts thank them and sign off with social media and email contact details.
